Associated Press)The civil code, published in 1865, declared that a child born to an Italian citizen was also an Italian citizen.However, a controversial law passed by the Italian government last year restricted citizenship for those born abroad.The Constitutional Court has now ruled in favour of the government after the new law was questioned by four judges.The court released a statement confirming its position, and is expected to give a more detailed verdict over the coming weeks.This ruling means that millions of Italian who have moved abroad over the years now risk denying
